name: Inhuman Conditions
summary: A two-player Blade Runner-inspired interrogation game where one player must detect if the other is human or robot.
rules_text: One player is Investigator, the other is Suspect. The Suspect secretly draws a role: Human, Patient Robot, or Violent Robot. Robots have a hidden speech restriction (e.g., may not mention people, may not use contractions). A penalty quirk card (e.g., apologize, use a double negative) is dealt face up. The Suspect also gets a background identity card for flavor. Setup: calibration - the Suspect must perform the penalty three times to the Investigator's satisfaction. Inducement - the Investigator asks about letter order on the Suspect's role card; humans have a maze to trace, robots have a simple list, creating a tell. The Investigator then places HUMAN and ROBOT stamps, starts a five-minute timer, and interviews using prompt cards from a topic deck. Robots must obey their restriction; if they break it they must do the penalty, on the honour system. Humans just converse naturally. The Investigator may stamp ROBOT at any time; if correct they win immediately. If time runs out, they must stamp HUMAN. Correct stamp wins for the Investigator, incorrect wins for the Suspect. Violent robots also win if they avoid detection until they can attack.
